defensible_basis: The cause-and-consequence syntax favors this pair while leaving its placement within the wider instructional collection non-authoritative.

source_observations.text: Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man. Don’t associate with one who harbors anger,
lest you learn his ways and ensnare your soul.

literary_form: surety prohibition with household consequence
deciding_marker_or_seam: The prohibition against hand pledges and debt surety is answered immediately by the rhetorical threat that the debtor bed will be taken away.
boundary_rationale: The prohibition against hand pledges and debt surety is answered immediately by the rhetorical threat that the debtor bed will be taken away.
rejected_alternative: Merging the pledge warning with 22:24-25 would erase the change from dangerous friendship to a discrete financial-social practice.
defensible_basis: The pair is a complete warning; retrieval must not imply a general legal ruling beyond its received wisdom context.

source_observations.text: Don’t you be one of those who strike hands, of those who are collateral for debts.
If you don’t have means to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?

literary_form: ancestral boundary-stone prohibition
deciding_marker_or_seam: The single prohibition against moving an ancient boundary marker names both the protected object and the ancestral act that established it before a new topic begins.
boundary_rationale: The single prohibition against moving an ancient boundary marker names both the protected object and the ancestral act that established it before a new topic begins.
rejected_alternative: Joining 22:28 to surety or skilled service would hide its self-contained land-boundary function, though a naked single verse would lose collection context.
defensible_basis: Its aphoristic closure is clear; mandatory parent and sibling hydration prevents isolated legal or historical overreading.

source_observations.text: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone which your fathers have set up.

literary_form: skilled-service observation and royal outcome
deciding_marker_or_seam: The rhetorical observation of a person skilled in work resolves in the contrast between standing before kings and standing before obscure people.
boundary_rationale: The rhetorical observation of a person skilled in work resolves in the contrast between standing before kings and standing before obscure people.
rejected_alternative: Attaching 22:29 to the boundary-stone warning would create a thematic cluster without a shared speaker, syntax, or repeated lexical frame.
defensible_basis: The saying is complete as a bicola, but it must surface with the named wise-sayings parent and nearby siblings.

source_observations.text: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.

literary_form: ruler-table appetite instruction
deciding_marker_or_seam: A when-clause places the learner at a ruler table; observe, restrain the throat, and distrust deceptive delicacies complete one high-stakes appetite instruction.
boundary_rationale: A when-clause places the learner at a ruler table; observe, restrain the throat, and distrust deceptive delicacies complete one high-stakes appetite instruction.
rejected_alternative: Joining through 23:5 would combine court-table self-control with the next instruction against exhausting oneself to acquire wealth.
defensible_basis: The scene and imperative chain close at 23:3, while the wider wise-sayings parent remains necessary context.

source_observations.text: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before you;
Don’t be desirous of his dainties, since they are deceitful food.

literary_form: wealth-pursuit prohibition with winged reversal
deciding_marker_or_seam: The command not to wear oneself out for riches is followed by a rhetorical glance and the eagle-wing image in which wealth vanishes.
boundary_rationale: The command not to wear oneself out for riches is followed by a rhetorical glance and the eagle-wing image in which wealth vanishes.
rejected_alternative: Absorbing 23:4-5 into the ruler-table scene would treat two distinct appetite objects as one instruction without a continuing situation.
defensible_basis: Imperative and image form a closed warning, although its economic language remains translation-sensitive evidence only.

source_observations.text: Don’t weary yourself to be rich. In your wisdom, show restraint.
Why do you set your eyes on that which is not? For it certainly sprouts wings like an eagle and flies in the sky.

literary_form: stingy-host meal warning
deciding_marker_or_seam: The evil-eyed host opens a meal scene; deceptive hospitality, inward calculation, and the guest vomiting the morsel and losing praise resolve the warning.
boundary_rationale: The evil-eyed host opens a meal scene; deceptive hospitality, inward calculation, and the guest vomiting the morsel and losing praise resolve the warning.
rejected_alternative: Extending to 23:9 would merge a narrated hospitality trap with a direct prohibition against speaking wisdom to a fool.
defensible_basis: The guest-host reversal is coherent, while the precise Hebrew description of the host is not used to select a preferred translation.

source_observations.text: Don’t eat the food of him who has a stingy eye, and don’t crave his delicacies,
You will vomit up the morsel which you have eaten and waste your pleasant words.

literary_form: audience-selection prohibition concerning a fool
deciding_marker_or_seam: The direct command not to speak within a fool hearing supplies its own reason: that audience will despise the prudence of the words.
boundary_rationale: The direct command not to speak within a fool hearing supplies its own reason: that audience will despise the prudence of the words.
rejected_alternative: Joining this aphorism to the stingy-host episode would confuse a speech-audience rule with the prior meal scene.
defensible_basis: The one-verse form is bounded but is never retrieved without parent and sibling hydration because its application is easy to overgeneralize.

source_observations.text: Don’t speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.

literary_form: boundary-and-orphan protection warning
deciding_marker_or_seam: Twin prohibitions protect the ancient boundary and orphan fields; the reason clause invokes their strong Redeemer who will plead against the intruder.
boundary_rationale: Twin prohibitions protect the ancient boundary and orphan fields; the reason clause invokes their strong Redeemer who will plead against the intruder.
rejected_alternative: Merging 23:10-11 with the fool-audience saying would rely only on adjacency and would detach the prohibition from its divine-reversal reason.
defensible_basis: The protected parties and Redeemer consequence close the pair, without converting wisdom language into a legal code.

source_observations.text: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone. Don’t encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
for their Defender is strong. He will plead their case against you.

literary_form: discipline exhortation with parental hope and envy restraint
deciding_marker_or_seam: Apply-heart and apply-ear imperatives open a discipline sequence; correction, parental gladness, guarded speech, and the final hope beyond envy close at 23:18.
boundary_rationale: Apply-heart and apply-ear imperatives open a discipline sequence; correction, parental gladness, guarded speech, and the final hope beyond envy close at 23:18.
rejected_alternative: Ending at 23:14 would isolate corporal-discipline language from the parental joy and future-oriented restraint that follow.
defensible_basis: Several linked admonitions form a movement, but the shift at 23:19 remains a plausible neighboring seam rather than certain compositional history.

source_observations.text: Apply your heart to instruction, and your ears to the words of knowledge.
Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.

literary_form: parental appeal against excess with father-mother joy
deciding_marker_or_seam: Hear and be wise renews direct address; the path command, warnings about drunkards and gluttons, renewed listen, wisdom acquisition, and parental joy conclude at 23:25.
boundary_rationale: Hear and be wise renews direct address; the path command, warnings about drunkards and gluttons, renewed listen, wisdom acquisition, and parental joy conclude at 23:25.
rejected_alternative: Keeping 23:12-25 as one unit would hide the renewed address at 23:19, yet cutting before 23:25 would sever conduct from its parental outcome.
defensible_basis: The sequence is linked by son and parent language, though its internal admonitions retain plausible smaller retrieval functions.

source_observations.text: Listen, my son, and be wise, and keep your heart on the right path!
Let your father and your mother be glad! Let her who bore you rejoice!

literary_form: heart-and-eyes appeal against sexual danger
deciding_marker_or_seam: My son give me your heart opens an intimate appeal; the eyes/path command is answered by pit and well images plus the prowler who increases betrayal.
boundary_rationale: My son give me your heart opens an intimate appeal; the eyes/path command is answered by pit and well images plus the prowler who increases betrayal.
rejected_alternative: Attaching 23:26-28 to the parental celebration at 23:24-25 would blur a new vocative appeal and its sustained danger imagery.
defensible_basis: The appeal and consequence form a complete warning without settling gender, ethics, or social history beyond the text.

source_observations.text: My son, give me your heart; and let your eyes keep in my ways.
Yes, she lies in wait like a robber, and increases the unfaithful among men.

literary_form: extended wine riddle, observation, and warning
deciding_marker_or_seam: Six 'who has' questions open; wine observation, sensory attraction, serpent consequence, distorted perception, and the drinker's final quoted resolve form a complete vignette.
boundary_rationale: Six 'who has' questions open; wine observation, sensory attraction, serpent consequence, distorted perception, and the drinker's final quoted resolve form a complete vignette.
rejected_alternative: Breaking at 23:31 would detach observation from consequences and compulsive closure.
defensible_basis: Low: formal question catalogue and narrative consequence.

source_observations.text: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?
“They hit me, and I was not hurt! They beat me, and I don’t feel it! When will I wake up? I can do it again. I will look for more.”

literary_form: envy prohibition concerning violent people
deciding_marker_or_seam: The command not to envy evil people or desire their company receives an immediate reason in their heart-plotted violence and trouble-speaking lips.
boundary_rationale: The command not to envy evil people or desire their company receives an immediate reason in their heart-plotted violence and trouble-speaking lips.
rejected_alternative: Joining 24:1-2 to house-building wisdom would combine an association warning with a new constructive metaphor and syntax.
defensible_basis: Prohibition and reason close together while remaining a child of the words-of-the-wise collection.

source_observations.text: Don’t be envious of evil men, neither desire to be with them;
for their hearts plot violence and their lips talk about mischief.

literary_form: wisdom-house and counsel-strength cluster
deciding_marker_or_seam: Wisdom builds and understanding establishes the house; knowledge fills rooms, then wise strength and counsel culminate in victory before the fool-at-the-gate contrast.
boundary_rationale: Wisdom builds and understanding establishes the house; knowledge fills rooms, then wise strength and counsel culminate in victory before the fool-at-the-gate contrast.
rejected_alternative: Ending at 24:4 would isolate the house image from its coordinated wisdom, knowledge, strength, and counsel expansion.
defensible_basis: The lexical wisdom chain supports the cluster, but the move from house to war counsel keeps confidence below the clearest formal units.

source_observations.text: Through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established;
Wisdom is too high for a fool. He doesn’t open his mouth in the gate.

literary_form: schemer and scoffer verdict pair
deciding_marker_or_seam: The person who plots evil receives the schemer designation, followed by a summary verdict that folly planning is sin and a scoffer is detestable.
boundary_rationale: The person who plots evil receives the schemer designation, followed by a summary verdict that folly planning is sin and a scoffer is detestable.
rejected_alternative: Merging these verdicts with the prior wisdom-house cluster would weaken the new subject and the compact naming-and-evaluation form.
defensible_basis: The pair is coherent as a character verdict without authorizing an ontology of persons or motives.

source_observations.text: One who plots to do evil will be called a schemer.
The schemes of folly are sin. The mocker is detested by men.

literary_form: crisis-strength and endangered-neighbor rescue instruction
deciding_marker_or_seam: Faintness in adversity tests strength, then rescue imperatives and the do-not-say defense culminate in the heart-weighing God who repays human work.
boundary_rationale: Faintness in adversity tests strength, then rescue imperatives and the do-not-say defense culminate in the heart-weighing God who repays human work.
rejected_alternative: Cutting after 24:10 would detach the crisis-strength maxim from the concrete rescue obligation that tests the claimed strength.
defensible_basis: The moral movement is strong, though whether 24:10 serves as its heading or an independent aphorism remains contestable.

source_observations.text: If you falter in the time of trouble, your strength is small.
If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this,” doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not give to every man according to his work?

literary_form: honey-to-wisdom analogy with future hope
deciding_marker_or_seam: The imperative to eat good honey supplies a tasted comparison for knowing wisdom; finding it yields a future and an uncut hope.
boundary_rationale: The imperative to eat good honey supplies a tasted comparison for knowing wisdom; finding it yields a future and an uncut hope.
rejected_alternative: Extending through 24:16 would merge an analogy about wisdom reward with a direct ambush prohibition against the righteous dwelling.
defensible_basis: Image, application, and future result complete the analogy while the semantic range of hope remains translation evidence only.

source_observations.text: My son, eat honey, for it is good, the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to your taste;
so you shall know wisdom to be to your soul. If you have found it, then there will be a reward: Your hope will not be cut off.

literary_form: ambush prohibition with sevenfold recovery contrast
deciding_marker_or_seam: The wicked addressee is forbidden to ambush or destroy the righteous home, because seven falls are answered by rising while calamity fells the wicked.
boundary_rationale: The wicked addressee is forbidden to ambush or destroy the righteous home, because seven falls are answered by rising while calamity fells the wicked.
rejected_alternative: Joining 24:15-16 to the honey analogy would conceal the addressee change and its prohibition-reversal structure.
defensible_basis: The warning is tightly reasoned, but seven functions rhetorically and is not turned into numerical doctrine.

source_observations.text: Don’t lay in wait, wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous. Don’t destroy his resting place;
for a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again, but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.

literary_form: enemy-downfall gloating prohibition
deciding_marker_or_seam: Do not rejoice when an enemy falls is paired with a heart warning and a reason: YHWH may see, disapprove, and turn anger away.
boundary_rationale: Do not rejoice when an enemy falls is paired with a heart warning and a reason: YHWH may see, disapprove, and turn anger away.
rejected_alternative: Absorbing the gloating warning into 24:15-16 would confuse the righteous persons recovery with the readers response to an enemys fall.
defensible_basis: Imperative, interior disposition, and divine response form a complete caution without settling later ethical reuse.

source_observations.text: Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls. Don’t let your heart be glad when he is overthrown,
lest Yahweh see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.

literary_form: evildoer-envy prohibition with extinguished future
deciding_marker_or_seam: The paired commands not to fret over evildoers or envy the wicked receive their reason in the absence of a future and the extinguished lamp.
boundary_rationale: The paired commands not to fret over evildoers or envy the wicked receive their reason in the absence of a future and the extinguished lamp.
rejected_alternative: Joining 24:19-20 to the enemy-fall warning would merge distinct emotional dangers and distinct divine-outcome reasons.
defensible_basis: The prohibition and lamp image close the unit, though future wording remains evidence rather than doctrinal authority.

source_observations.text: Don’t fret yourself because of evildoers, neither be envious of the wicked;
for there will be no reward to the evil man. The lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.

literary_form: fear and non-rebellion instruction concerning YHWH and king
deciding_marker_or_seam: My son renews address with fear of YHWH and king and a ban on joining change-seekers; sudden ruin and unknowable destruction close the instruction.
boundary_rationale: My son renews address with fear of YHWH and king and a ban on joining change-seekers; sudden ruin and unknowable destruction close the instruction.
rejected_alternative: Extending backward to 24:19 would blur the renewed vocative and the distinct paired authorities named in the final saying.
defensible_basis: The address and consequence provide formal closure without deciding politics, chronology, or a canonical theory of government.

source_observations.text: My son, fear Yahweh and the king. Don’t join those who are rebellious,
for their calamity will rise suddenly. Who knows what destruction may come from them both?

literary_form: supplement superscription with partiality and rebuke contrast
deciding_marker_or_seam: These also are sayings of the wise opens a supplement, condemns judicial partiality, then contrasts curse and abhorrence for corrupt acquittal with delight and blessing for righteous rebuke.
boundary_rationale: These also are sayings of the wise opens a supplement, condemns judicial partiality, then contrasts curse and abhorrence for corrupt acquittal with delight and blessing for righteous rebuke.
rejected_alternative: Keeping 24:23-29 as one civic-neighbor cluster would let the supplement heading erase four complete local saying forms.
defensible_basis: The superscription and paired judicial outcomes make a coherent opening child while 24:23-34 remains its collection parent.

source_observations.text: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.
but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and a rich blessing will come on them.

literary_form: apt-and-honest-answer kiss aphorism
deciding_marker_or_seam: The single comparison equates an honest or right answer with a kiss on the lips, completing both image and evaluated speech act within one bicola.
boundary_rationale: The single comparison equates an honest or right answer with a kiss on the lips, completing both image and evaluated speech act within one bicola.
rejected_alternative: Absorbing 24:26 into the judicial contrast or work-sequencing instruction would rely on broad social conduct rather than continuing syntax or imagery.
defensible_basis: The aphorism is complete but mandatory 24:23-34 parent and sibling hydration prevents naked retrieval.

source_observations.text: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.

literary_form: work-before-house sequencing instruction
deciding_marker_or_seam: Prepare field work, make it ready, and afterward build the house form an ordered imperative sequence with its temporal priority stated inside the verse.
boundary_rationale: Prepare field work, make it ready, and afterward build the house form an ordered imperative sequence with its temporal priority stated inside the verse.
rejected_alternative: Joining 24:27 to the apt-answer saying or false-witness pair would blur a self-contained work-order instruction with unrelated neighbor speech.
defensible_basis: The command sequence is complete but receives mandatory supplement-parent hydration as a one-verse child.

source_observations.text: Prepare your work outside, and get your fields ready. Afterwards, build your house.

literary_form: false-witness and non-retaliation neighbor instruction pair
deciding_marker_or_seam: Negative commands forbid groundless testimony and deceptive lips against a neighbor, then directly reject repayment in kind for what another has done.
boundary_rationale: Negative commands forbid groundless testimony and deceptive lips against a neighbor, then directly reject repayment in kind for what another has done.
rejected_alternative: Keeping 24:28-29 inside a 24:23-29 lump would hide the explicit neighbor-witness and retaliation sequence that closes before the field vignette.
defensible_basis: The shared neighbor-harm address binds the pair, while the prior whole-cluster position remains preserved as an appeal.

source_observations.text: Don’t be a witness against your neighbor without cause. Don’t deceive with your lips.
Don’t say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”

literary_form: first-person sluggard-field observation and lesson
deciding_marker_or_seam: 'I went by the field' introduces a first-person scene; observed neglect, reflective seeing, and repeated sleep/poverty conclusion form a self-contained vignette.
boundary_rationale: 'I went by the field' introduces a first-person scene; observed neglect, reflective seeing, and repeated sleep/poverty conclusion form a self-contained vignette.
rejected_alternative: Separating the final poverty saying would detach the lesson learned from the observed field.
defensible_basis: Low: scene and explicit reflection close the supplement.

source_observations.text: I went by the field of the sluggard, by the vineyard of the man void of understanding.
so your poverty will come as a robber and your want as an armed man.

literary_form: Hezekiah-copy superscription with opening royal-court instruction
deciding_marker_or_seam: The explicit copied-Solomon superscription opens a new collection; divine concealment/royal searching, removal of wicked court influence, and self-lowering before a king close at the court displacement warning.
boundary_rationale: The explicit copied-Solomon superscription opens a new collection; divine concealment/royal searching, removal of wicked court influence, and self-lowering before a king close at the court displacement warning.
rejected_alternative: Prov.25.1 alone would isolate the title; ending on chapter number would be irrelevant because the unit closes at royal audience conduct.
defensible_basis: Low-medium: clear collection opening and concentrated royal vocabulary.

source_observations.text: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
for it is better that it be said to you, “Come up here,” than that you should be put lower in the presence of the prince, whom your eyes have seen.

literary_form: dispute, confidentiality, apt speech, faithful messenger, false gift, and patient persuasion cluster
deciding_marker_or_seam: Do-not-rush-to-court opens; private dispute handling, fitting words, faithful messenger, false boasting, and patient tongue all concern responsible communication in contested relations.
boundary_rationale: Do-not-rush-to-court opens; private dispute handling, fitting words, faithful messenger, false boasting, and patient tongue all concern responsible communication in contested relations.
rejected_alternative: One image per chunk would obscure the dispute-to-persuasion communication chain.
defensible_basis: Medium: messenger and gift images broaden the legal frame.

source_observations.text: Don’t be hasty in bringing charges to court. What will you do in the end when your neighbor shames you?
By patience a ruler is persuaded. A soft tongue breaks the bone.

literary_form: paired moderation sayings on honey and neighbor access
deciding_marker_or_seam: Finding honey introduces a sufficiency warning ending in vomiting; the matched too-much pattern then applies measured presence to a neighbors house.
boundary_rationale: Finding honey introduces a sufficiency warning ending in vomiting; the matched too-much pattern then applies measured presence to a neighbors house.
rejected_alternative: Keeping 25:16-22 whole would hide this deliberate excess analogy before the form shifts to witness and reliability images.
defensible_basis: The paired moderation logic supports retrieval, while the comparison does not erase the distinct social object of the second saying.

source_observations.text: Have you found honey? Eat as much as is sufficient for you, lest you eat too much, and vomit it.
Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, lest he be weary of you, and hate you.

literary_form: harmful-neighbor comparison triad
deciding_marker_or_seam: False witness becomes club, sword, and arrow; unreliable trust becomes a bad tooth and unsteady foot; misplaced song becomes garment removal and acid on alkali.
boundary_rationale: False witness becomes club, sword, and arrow; unreliable trust becomes a bad tooth and unsteady foot; misplaced song becomes garment removal and acid on alkali.
rejected_alternative: Splitting each verse would lose the consecutive harmful-comparison triad, but attaching enemy care would add a new imperative and YHWH result.
defensible_basis: The images form a plausible cluster even though their topics differ, so confidence remains medium rather than high.

source_observations.text: A man who gives false testimony against his neighbor is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.

literary_form: enemy-care instruction with burning-coals image
deciding_marker_or_seam: Conditional enemy hunger and thirst receive food-and-water imperatives; the burning-coals consequence and YHWH reward complete the instruction.
boundary_rationale: Conditional enemy hunger and thirst receive food-and-water imperatives; the burning-coals consequence and YHWH reward complete the instruction.
rejected_alternative: Joining 25:21-22 to the prior comparison triad would detach the explicit condition and positive commands from their own outcome.
defensible_basis: The syntax bounds the pair, while the coals image and later reuse remain interpretation evidence rather than seam authority.

source_observations.text: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink;
for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and Yahweh will reward you.

literary_form: social provocation and self-restraint closing cluster
deciding_marker_or_seam: Wind/rain and secret tongue open; contentious-house contrast, good news/cold water, compromised righteous spring, excess honey/honor, and wall-less self-control close the sequence.
boundary_rationale: Wind/rain and secret tongue open; contentious-house contrast, good news/cold water, compromised righteous spring, excess honey/honor, and wall-less self-control close the sequence.
rejected_alternative: A chapter-sized fallback is rejected; the wall-less-city self-rule image provides the positive cadence.
defensible_basis: T467 chapter-coincident risk: the social/self-restraint theme is loose.

source_observations.text: The north wind produces rain; so a backbiting tongue brings an angry face.
Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.

literary_form: extended fool catalogue
deciding_marker_or_seam: Repeated 'fool' vocabulary governs honor, curse, rod, answer/no-answer paradox, messenger, proverb, and self-estimation, culminating in the person wise in own eyes as worse than a fool.
boundary_rationale: Repeated 'fool' vocabulary governs honor, curse, rod, answer/no-answer paradox, messenger, proverb, and self-estimation, culminating in the person wise in own eyes as worse than a fool.
rejected_alternative: Splitting 26:4-5 would destroy the deliberate paired tension; individual fool sayings belong to the catalogue.
defensible_basis: Medium: literary grouping does not harmonize the answer/no-answer pair.

source_observations.text: Like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.
Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

literary_form: sluggard caricature catalogue
deciding_marker_or_seam: The lion excuse introduces four consecutive sluggard images: door/bed turning, hand in dish, and self-estimated wisdom.
boundary_rationale: The lion excuse introduces four consecutive sluggard images: door/bed turning, hand in dish, and self-estimated wisdom.
rejected_alternative: One image per unit would atomize a named-character catalogue.
defensible_basis: Low: four consecutive sluggard sayings.

source_observations.text: The sluggard says, “There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!”
The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with discretion.

literary_form: meddling, deception, quarrel, gossip, hatred, and flattering-mouth catalogue
deciding_marker_or_seam: Meddling in another's quarrel opens; madman's deceptive joke, fuel/fire gossip, disguised hatred, pit/stone reversal, and lying/flattering mouth form escalating destructive speech.
boundary_rationale: Meddling in another's quarrel opens; madman's deceptive joke, fuel/fire gossip, disguised hatred, pit/stone reversal, and lying/flattering mouth form escalating destructive speech.
rejected_alternative: The chapter seam is not the basis; repeated quarrel/gossip/lying-mouth vocabulary supplies the closure.
defensible_basis: T467 chapter-coincident risk is mitigated by an unusually dense destructive-speech chain.

source_observations.text: Like one who grabs a dog’s ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.
A lying tongue hates those it hurts; and a flattering mouth works ruin.

literary_form: boasting, rebuke, provocation, jealousy, and loyal-friendship cluster
deciding_marker_or_seam: Do-not-boast opens; praise, fool's provocation, jealousy, open rebuke, faithful wounds, appetite, wandering, perfume/counsel, and enduring friend/neighbor loyalty culminate in near-neighbor preference.
boundary_rationale: Do-not-boast opens; praise, fool's provocation, jealousy, open rebuke, faithful wounds, appetite, wandering, perfume/counsel, and enduring friend/neighbor loyalty culminate in near-neighbor preference.
rejected_alternative: Extracting friendship aphorisms would remove their contrast with praise, rebuke, and provocation.
defensible_basis: High: appetite and wandering images loosen the friendship frame.

source_observations.text: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster. A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.

literary_form: wise son, prudence, surety, contentious housemate, friendship sharpening, stewardship, appetite, heart, and refining cluster
deciding_marker_or_seam: 'My son, be wise' opens; prudent refuge and relational/household images lead through sharpening, stewardship, insatiable appetite, heart reflection, and praise-as-crucible to the fool who resists refining.
boundary_rationale: 'My son, be wise' opens; prudent refuge and relational/household images lead through sharpening, stewardship, insatiable appetite, heart reflection, and praise-as-crucible to the fool who resists refining.
rejected_alternative: A one-verse treatment would erase repeated testing/knowing-character concerns.
defensible_basis: High: several independent sayings are conservatively kept under the collection parent.

source_observations.text: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.
Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.

literary_form: flock-and-household stewardship instruction
deciding_marker_or_seam: Imperatives to know flock condition open; impermanent riches and crown yield to seasonal fodder, lamb/goat provision, and household/maidens support.
boundary_rationale: Imperatives to know flock condition open; impermanent riches and crown yield to seasonal fodder, lamb/goat provision, and household/maidens support.
rejected_alternative: Separating resource-cycle lines would fragment one practical stewardship instruction.
defensible_basis: Low: sustained flock/economic cycle and household outcome.

source_observations.text: Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds,
There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.

literary_form: righteous courage, social order, Torah, poverty/wealth, integrity, and public rule cluster
deciding_marker_or_seam: Wicked flight/righteous boldness opens; national rulers, oppressive poor, Torah keeping, justice-seeking, usury, prayer, integrity, inheritance, and righteous triumph develop public moral order.
boundary_rationale: Wicked flight/righteous boldness opens; national rulers, oppressive poor, Torah keeping, justice-seeking, usury, prayer, integrity, inheritance, and righteous triumph develop public moral order.
rejected_alternative: A chapter-sized unit is rejected, while isolated Torah or poverty verses would lose the governance sequence.
defensible_basis: High: public-order linkage is broad and exact endpoint disputed.

source_observations.text: The wicked flee when no one pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.

literary_form: confession, fear, oppressive rule, guilt, integrity, partiality, greed, rebuke, family, trust, generosity, and righteous-public reversal cluster
deciding_marker_or_seam: Conceal/confess sin opens; fear/hardening, bad ruler, bloodguilt, integrity, wealth/partiality, greed, rebuke, parental robbery, proud trust, poor generosity, and wicked/righteous public reversal close the chapter's second movement.
boundary_rationale: Conceal/confess sin opens; fear/hardening, bad ruler, bloodguilt, integrity, wealth/partiality, greed, rebuke, parental robbery, proud trust, poor generosity, and wicked/righteous public reversal close the chapter's second movement.
rejected_alternative: Chapter number alone is rejected; confession/exposure and wicked/righteous hiding/emergence form a broad reversal envelope.
defensible_basis: T467 chapter-coincident risk: the reversal envelope is real but many internal clusters compete.

source_observations.text: He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous thrive.

literary_form: resistance to correction, righteous rule, justice, speech conflict, and kingly care for poor cluster
deciding_marker_or_seam: Repeated-reproof hardening opens; righteous/wicked rule, wisdom/shame, king by justice, flattery, snares, singing, poor-rights knowledge, mockers, fool/wise conflict, and king judging poor culminate in established throne.
boundary_rationale: Repeated-reproof hardening opens; righteous/wicked rule, wisdom/shame, king by justice, flattery, snares, singing, poor-rights knowledge, mockers, fool/wise conflict, and king judging poor culminate in established throne.
rejected_alternative: Splitting royal sayings from justice/poor sayings would weaken the rule-and-response sequence.
defensible_basis: High: speech-conflict sayings interrupt the governance chain.

source_observations.text: He who is often rebuked and stiffens his neck will be destroyed suddenly, with no remedy.
The king who fairly judges the poor, his throne shall be established forever.

literary_form: discipline, law/vision, servant, anger, speech haste, pride, complicity, fear, ruler, and justice collection closure
deciding_marker_or_seam: Rod/reproof and child discipline open; wicked increase, no-vision/Torah, servant correction, anger, hasty speech, pride, theft complicity, fear of man, ruler-seeking, and righteous/wicked mutual abhorrence close the copied collection.
boundary_rationale: Rod/reproof and child discipline open; wicked increase, no-vision/Torah, servant correction, anger, hasty speech, pride, theft complicity, fear of man, ruler-seeking, and righteous/wicked mutual abhorrence close the copied collection.
rejected_alternative: The chapter seam is not sufficient; the unit ends because 30:1 explicitly introduces Agur and a new speaker-text complex.
defensible_basis: Medium-high: endpoint is hard, internal cluster remains composite.

source_observations.text: The rod of correction gives wisdom, but a child left to himself causes shame to his mother.
A dishonest man detests the righteous, and the upright in their ways detest the wicked.

literary_form: Agur superscription, confession of limitation, questions, and word-of-God warning
deciding_marker_or_seam: Agur's named superscription opens; first-person weariness/ignorance, ascent-and-creation questions, and tested-word refuge culminate in a prohibition on adding.
boundary_rationale: Agur's named superscription opens; first-person weariness/ignorance, ascent-and-creation questions, and tested-word refuge culminate in a prohibition on adding.
rejected_alternative: Prov.30.1 alone would isolate a textually pressured superscription from its speaker's confession.
defensible_basis: Medium: names/addressees and translation are difficult; no preferred reading is selected.

source_observations.text: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, the revelation: the man says to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
Don’t you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.

hold.question: Should Proverbs 30:1 remain attached to the confession and word warning in 30:2-6, or function as a heading over a 30:2-6 speech child within 30:1-9?

literary_form: two-request prayer for truth and daily sufficiency
deciding_marker_or_seam: 'Two things I have asked' provides a number frame; removal of falsehood and neither poverty nor riches are motivated by paired denial/forgetting risks.
boundary_rationale: 'Two things I have asked' provides a number frame; removal of falsehood and neither poverty nor riches are motivated by paired denial/forgetting risks.
rejected_alternative: Splitting the two requests would violate the explicit number frame.
defensible_basis: Low: explicit petition and motive closure.

source_observations.text: “Two things I have asked of you. Don’t deny me before I die.
lest I be full, deny you, and say, ‘Who is Yahweh?’ or lest I be poor, and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.

literary_form: servant-slander prohibition with curse consequence
deciding_marker_or_seam: The direct prohibition against slandering a servant to a master carries its own stated consequence: the servant may curse the slanderer and expose guilt.
boundary_rationale: The direct prohibition against slandering a servant to a master carries its own stated consequence: the servant may curse the slanderer and expose guilt.
rejected_alternative: Joining 30:10 to the generation catalogue at 30:11 would suppress the new repeated generation subject and its explicit fourfold form.
defensible_basis: The one-verse prohibition is complete but must be hydrated with the Agur parent and adjacent numerical siblings.

source_observations.text: “Don’t slander a servant to his master, lest he curse you, and you be held guilty.

literary_form: fourfold corrupt-generation catalogue
deciding_marker_or_seam: Four consecutive clauses begin with a generation: cursing parents, self-purity without cleansing, lofty eyes, and teeth or jaws that devour the vulnerable.
boundary_rationale: Four consecutive clauses begin with a generation: cursing parents, self-purity without cleansing, lofty eyes, and teeth or jaws that devour the vulnerable.
rejected_alternative: Absorbing verse 10 would place an independent second-person prohibition inside a formally repeated four-member subject catalogue.
defensible_basis: The repeated generation opening provides strong form evidence without turning the social portraits into claims about chronology.

source_observations.text: There is a generation that curses their father, and doesn’t bless their mother.
There is a generation whose teeth are like swords, and their jaws like knives, to devour the poor from the earth, and the needy from among men.

literary_form: three-and-four insatiables numerical saying
deciding_marker_or_seam: The leech image opens into the explicit three things, yes four never-satisfied formula, whose members are Sheol, barren womb, waterless earth, and fire.
boundary_rationale: The leech image opens into the explicit three things, yes four never-satisfied formula, whose members are Sheol, barren womb, waterless earth, and fire.
rejected_alternative: Carrying the numerical unit through verse 17 would add an unnumbered filial-eye warning after the fourth member has already closed the count.
defensible_basis: The count and four unsated images form a stable unit while the imagery remains interpretation evidence only.

source_observations.text: “The leech has two daughters: ‘Give, give.’ “There are three things that are never satisfied; four that don’t say, ‘Enough!’:
Sheol, the barren womb, the earth that is not satisfied with water, and the fire that doesn’t say, ‘Enough!’

literary_form: filial-eye contempt warning and carrion consequence
deciding_marker_or_seam: The eye that mocks a father and scorns maternal obedience becomes a new grammatical subject, followed by ravens and eagle young consuming that eye.
boundary_rationale: The eye that mocks a father and scorns maternal obedience becomes a new grammatical subject, followed by ravens and eagle young consuming that eye.
rejected_alternative: Joining verse 17 to the insatiables list relies on a devouring echo even though the three-and-four formula closes with fire at verse 16.
defensible_basis: The saying is self-contained but never retrieved without the Agur collection parent and neighboring catalogue context.

source_observations.text: “The eye that mocks at his father, and scorns obedience to his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, the young eagles shall eat it.

literary_form: three/four wondrous ways catalogue with adulterous-woman analogy
deciding_marker_or_seam: 'Three things...four' opens; eagle, serpent, ship, and man-with-maiden ways culminate in the adulterous woman's erased-trace comparison.
boundary_rationale: 'Three things...four' opens; eagle, serpent, ship, and man-with-maiden ways culminate in the adulterous woman's erased-trace comparison.
rejected_alternative: Separating 30:20 would detach the interpretive analogy from the four-way riddle.
defensible_basis: Medium: the analogy's semantic force is disputed, but its literary attachment is strong.

source_observations.text: “There are three things which are too amazing for me, four which I don’t understand:
“So is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats and wipes her mouth, and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’

literary_form: three/four socially unbearable reversals catalogue
deciding_marker_or_seam: 'For three things the earth trembles, and under four' governs servant, fool, unloved wife, and servant-girl reversals.
boundary_rationale: 'For three things the earth trembles, and under four' governs servant, fool, unloved wife, and servant-girl reversals.
rejected_alternative: No member of the numbered list is split from its governing formula.
defensible_basis: Low: explicit numerical frame.

source_observations.text: “For three things the earth trembles, and under four, it can’t bear up:
for an unloved woman when she is married, and a servant who is heir to her mistress.

literary_form: four small-but-wise creatures catalogue
deciding_marker_or_seam: 'Four things are little...but exceedingly wise' governs ants, hyraxes, locusts, and lizard, each with a functional observation.
boundary_rationale: 'Four things are little...but exceedingly wise' governs ants, hyraxes, locusts, and lizard, each with a functional observation.
rejected_alternative: One animal per chunk would atomize the explicit fourfold catalogue.
defensible_basis: Low: explicit number and evaluative frame.

source_observations.text: “There are four things which are little on the earth, but they are exceedingly wise:
You can catch a lizard with your hands, yet it is in kings’ palaces.

literary_form: three-and-four stately walkers catalogue
deciding_marker_or_seam: The three things, yes four stately walkers formula enumerates lion, the translation-disputed second animal, male goat, and a king against whom there is no rising up, closing at 30:31.
boundary_rationale: The three things, yes four stately walkers formula enumerates lion, the translation-disputed second animal, male goat, and a king against whom there is no rising up, closing at 30:31.
rejected_alternative: Carrying the list through 30:33 would merge its explicit four-member count with a separate closing admonition against self-exaltation and strife.
defensible_basis: The numbered form is clear, while the disputed animal rendering is preserved as translation uncertainty and not used as authority.

source_observations.text: “There are three things which are stately in their march, four which are stately in going:
the greyhound; the male goat; and the king against whom there is no rising up.

literary_form: anti-exaltation and anti-strife closing counsel
deciding_marker_or_seam: A conditional admission of foolish self-exaltation commands hand-to-mouth restraint; three parallel pressings then move from milk and nose to anger producing strife.
boundary_rationale: A conditional admission of foolish self-exaltation commands hand-to-mouth restraint; three parallel pressings then move from milk and nose to anger producing strife.
rejected_alternative: Attaching 30:32-33 to the stately-walkers list would weaken the new conditional address and its independent threefold cause-effect analogy.
defensible_basis: The counsel completes Agurs sequence, but whole 30:29-33 retrieval remains a documented alternate treatment.

source_observations.text: “If you have done foolishly in lifting up yourself, or if you have thought evil, put your hand over your mouth.
For as the churning of milk produces butter, and the wringing of the nose produces blood, so the forcing of wrath produces strife.”

literary_form: Lemuel superscription and maternal royal instruction
deciding_marker_or_seam: The named Lemuel oracle/instruction from his mother opens; triple 'what, my son' appeal, warning about strength and wine, and imperatives to speak/judge for vulnerable people close at 31:9.
boundary_rationale: The named Lemuel oracle/instruction from his mother opens; triple 'what, my son' appeal, warning about strength and wine, and imperatives to speak/judge for vulnerable people close at 31:9.
rejected_alternative: Prov.31.1 alone would detach the superscription from the maternal royal instruction; merging the acrostic would ignore a new alphabetic form.
defensible_basis: Medium: names and translation are pressured, but speaker/addressee and instruction closure are clear.

source_observations.text: The words of King Lemuel—the revelation which his mother taught him:
Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.”

hold.question: Should Proverbs 31:1 be integral to the maternal royal instruction in 31:2-9, or serve as a heading over an internal 31:2-9 instruction child?

literary_form: alphabetic poem praising a capable/valiant woman
deciding_marker_or_seam: The rhetorical 'who can find' opens a self-contained portrait; the Hebrew alphabetic sequence governs twenty-two verses and closes with public praise for the fruit of her hands.
boundary_rationale: The rhetorical 'who can find' opens a self-contained portrait; the Hebrew alphabetic sequence governs twenty-two verses and closes with public praise for the fruit of her hands.
rejected_alternative: Topical or one-verse subdivision would fragment the governing alphabetic poem.
defensible_basis: Low literary seam; Hebrew wording, gender/social interpretation, and alphabetic evidence remain non-authorizing.

source_observations.text: Who can find a worthy woman? For her value is far above rubies.
Give her of the fruit of her hands! Let her works praise her in the gates!
